The operators own dedicated page for this facility, refetched directly this session, gives 26 MW of capacity, 96,129 square feet, and a 20 acre private campus, describing a 6 inch concrete roof deck able to sustain over 190 mph winds and a DoubleDense technology supporting loads up to 1,000 watts per square foot with immersion cooling. A data center industry aggregator directorys general area listing independently names this exact facility, Skybox Houston One under operator Skybox Datacenters, at 22000 Franz Road, Houston, TX 77449, which this session applies as this rows address, describing it as a purpose built, wholesale data center designed for wind resistance. This session refetched the operators own dedicated Chicago area location page directly and found it states, in its own words, ownership as Skybox Powered by Prologis, describing a joint venture. Prologis is a large, publicly traded industrial and logistics real estate company. No second, independent source describing this relationship was found this session, though the statement comes directly from the operators own site, the highest tier source under this projects source hierarchy. The company also confirms Chicago, Santa Clara, California, and Northern Virginia among its completed projects, with projects underway in Austin, Dallas, and Wichita Falls, Texas. No founding date or headquarters address for the company itself were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Skybox Houston One in Harris County, Texas, is operated by Skybox, but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

Skybox Houston One holds 1 published certification: LEED (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Texas has 23 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 15 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 399.41 MW.
